The mapping layer itself needs validation - wrong reason codes violate even when scores are correct.

drills.q: AML alert queue: 10k alerts/month at 94% FP rate. Where do ML models help first?
drills.a: Alert scoring/prioritization: rank queues so investigators clear true positives earlier (ranking metric, not calibration); entity resolution merges duplicate subjects; graph analytics surface networks invisible transaction-by-transaction. Capacity math stays human: SAR narratives and referrals remain analyst-owned.

drills.q: Fraud score distribution compressed toward the safe zone over 6 weeks while chargeback lag hides labels. Diagnose.
drills.a: Classic adversarial probing signature: adversary tested until boundary softened. Actions: switch evaluation to delayed-feedback-aware metrics, compare feature-drift attribution (boundary-concentrated shift = hostile), rotate champion/retrain on recent confirmed patterns, add rules for observed new patterns, verify kill-switch to rules-only mode works.

drills.q: Assets: 400 Treasuries (0%), 300 retail (75%), 200 corporate unrated (100%). RWA and density?
drills.a: RWA = 0 + 225 + 200 = 425. Density = 425/900 = 47.2%. Same assets, different mix - composition IS capital strategy.

drills.q: CET1 = 150, used RWA = 1,800. Ratio vs the 7% all-in minimum? Surplus in dollars?
drills.a: Ratio = 150/1800 = 8.33%. Minimum needs 0.07 x 1800 = 126. Surplus = 24mm. Note G-SIBs with SCB face low-teens effective requirements - check which requirement applies before celebrating.

drills.q: IRB RWA = 1,000; standardized RWA = 1,600. Full-phase floor: which RWA is used?
drills.a: Floor = 0.725 x 1600 = 1160 > 1000 -> floor binds, use 1160. The internal models' 20% advantage shrinks to nothing beyond the floor; at mid phase-in (e.g., 65%) floor = 1040, still binding.

drills.q: HQLA: Level1 = 300, Level2A = 150. Compute capped HQLA.
drills.a: L2A cap = 40% of total HQLA: solve L2A <= 0.4(300+L2A) -> L2A <= 200. 150 < 200 so uncapped: HQLA = 450. If net outflows were 400, LCR = 112.5% - pass.

drills.q: Why can a bank pass LCR/NSFR and still fail in days? Give the 2023 example mechanics.
drills.a: Metrics assume runoff rates over 30 days/1 year calibrated to history. SVB: ~90% uninsured deposits ran within ~48 hours via mobile banking after a Twitter-era panic - far faster than any assumption - while HTM unrealized losses (~$15B+) meant selling HQLA created capital holes. Speed + rate risk broke calibration.

drills.q: Your desk's IMM capital beats SA by 40%. Bank-wide benefit under full output floor?
drills.a: Bank-wide modeled RWA still cannot drop below 72.5% of SA total, so the whole-bank benefit caps at 27.5% regardless of desk-level wins. Desk optimization matters only where aggregate modeled RWA sits above the floor.

drills.q: Name two reasons Basel II's IRB amplified procyclicality.
drills.a: 1) Through-the-cycle PD/LGD estimates updated downward in booms expanded credit exactly when risks built; 2) downturn LGDs/PDs realized point-in-time in busts forced capital raises at market bottoms (fire-sale dynamics). Basel IV's floors + revised SA reduce model-driven amplitude.

drills.q: What did the RCAP/RWA dispersion studies show and what reform did they trigger?
drills.a: Near-identical portfolios carried roughly 2x different RWA across banks depending on internal-model choices - undermining comparability and trust. Triggered Basel IV: revised SA as benchmark, IRB input floors, and the 72.5% output floor capping model variance.

drills.q: S=100, K=100, T=1y, r=5%, vol=20%. Roughly price the call and state the hedge ratio.
drills.a: Call ~ 10.45; delta ~ 0.64 -> hold short ~64 shares per long call. Put via parity ~ 5.57. These are the canonical sanity numbers every desk interview expects cold.

drills.q: Put via parity: C=8.20, S=102, K=100, r=4%, T=0.5y, no dividends. Price?
drills.a: P = C - S + K*e^{-rT} = 8.20 - 102 + 100*e^{-0.02} = 8.20 - 102 + 98.02 = 4.22. Parity holds regardless of model - it's pure forward arithmetic; violations beyond costs are free money (conversion/reversal desks live here).

drills.q: Long call, delta-hedged daily. Week's realized vol 28% annualized vs entry implied 20%, average gamma*S^2 product constant at 0.5*0.0188*10000. Estimate the week's hedged P&L direction and magnitude per contract.
drills.a: Daily edge ~ 0.5*Gamma*S^2*(0.28^2-0.20^2)/252 = 0.5*0.0188*10000*(0.0484)/252 ~ $18/day -> ~$90/week positive. Realized exceeded implied: gamma earnings beat theta rent. Direction certain, magnitude path-dependent (gamma realized on actual wiggles).

drills.q: Rank vega: 1-week ATM, 2-year ATM, 3-month 20-delta wing. Explain.
drills.a: 2y ATM >> 3m wing > 1w ATM. Vega scales with sqrt(T) and peaks ATM: 2y/1w ratio ~ sqrt(104) ~ 10x+. Wings have less vega than same-tenor ATM but more volga - that's why tail desks bucket by strike region, not one net vega.

drills.q: MC prices a deep OTM barrier option. Control variate against terminal asset barely reduces SE. Why and what instead?
drills.a: Payoff is nearly orthogonal to S_T (indicator-like, far from strike): correlation rho~0 kills the 1/(1-rho^2) reduction. Switch controls to integrated variance / time-of-hit proxies for barrier-type payoffs, use importance sampling toward the barrier, or conditional Brownian-bridge hit probabilities.

drills.q: A digital's bump-and-revalue delta flips sign as you shrink the bump from 0.10 to 0.01. Diagnose.
drills.a: Classic kink problem: central differences across the payoff discontinuity mix probability mass inconsistently - bump size determines which paths straddle the cliff, so 'Greeks' track numerics not sensitivities. Fix: smooth the digital into a narrow call spread (document width), or use likelihood-ratio method.

drills.q: Why does local vol misprice forward-variance agreements even though it fits today's smile exactly?
drills.a: Local vol implies forward vols locked deterministically to today's surface - future smile evolves predictably from current one. Empirically forward vol moves independently (vol-of-vol), so LV systematically biases FVA/VIX-product hedges. Need stochastic-vol dynamics where future variance is its own random variable.

drills.q: EUR rates are -0.5%. What happens to optimal early exercise of American puts vs the classic textbook?
drills.a: Negative carry inverts logic: holding cash now costs money, so waiting to exercise earns negative interest - earlier exercise becomes MORE attractive, pushing the exercise boundary UP toward ATM. Post-2015 European markets forced libraries to handle this; textbooks assuming positive r silently broke.

drills.q: Trader quotes '32 at 33' in vol points for a 3-month 90-strike put. Why quote vol instead of premium?
drills.a: Vol is the standardized unit: separates market's volatility view from noise in spot/rate/dividend inputs, enables direct comparison across strikes/expiries, and makes Greeks coherent (vega/gamma computed consistently). Premium re-derived mechanically once conventions are fixed - the trade IS in vol points.

drills.q: Best ask 100.02 with 300 shares, next 100.03 with 450. You buy 500 market. Fill VWAP?
drills.a: 300 @ 100.02 + 200 @ 100.03 -> VWAP = (300*100.02 + 200*100.03)/500 = 100.024. Slippage vs arrival mid (assume 100.01): 1.4 cents on 100.015 mid ~ 1.4bp - the cost of walking one extra level.

drills.q: Daily vol is 2%, ADV is 5M shares, you trade 250k in one day. Square-root impact estimate with Y=0.8?
drills.a: Participation Q/V = 0.05; dp ~ 0.8 * 2% * sqrt(0.05) = 0.8*2%*0.224 ~ 36bp. Note sqrt: doubling to 500k only raises it to ~51bp (+41%), not double.

drills.q: Serial covariance of daily price changes is -0.0004. Estimate effective spread.
drills.a: Roll: cov = -(s/2)^2 -> s = 2*sqrt(0.0004) = 0.04. Effective spread ~ 4 cents. Caveat: estimator fails if prices trended over the sample (positive covariance masks the bounce).

drills.q: Your passive buy at the bid keeps filling right before down-moves. Diagnose and give two fixes.
drills.a: Adverse selection / toxicity: informed flow targets your quote. Fixes: (1) markout analysis by regime/time to find when your queue gets picked; cancel or widen during toxic windows; (2) skew quotes with inventory/signal (Avellaneda-Stoikov style) and shift toward taker execution when signal decay beats spread savings.

drills.q: Signal half-life is 90 seconds. Maker saves ~1.5bp round trip but queue wait averages 3 minutes. Aggressive or passive?
drills.a: Aggressive: waiting 3 minutes for ~1.5bp while a 90-second-half-life alpha decays means most of the edge evaporates before fill probability builds. Rule of thumb: go passive only when expected queue time << alpha half-life; otherwise pay the ~1.35bp taker cost.

drills.q: A backtest claims Sharpe 3.5 with fills at bar-close mid, trading 2% of ADV per signal, 50 trades/day. First three things you check?
drills.a: (1) Cost math: 2% participation x sqrt-law + saved half-spreads x 100 sides/day vs gross return per trade. (2) Latency: signal-at-close executed AT close assumes zero drift toward your own alpha. (3) Adverse selection on any simulated passive fills. Only then look at purge/embargo/trial-count statistics.

drills.q: Why do PFOF wholesalers pay brokers for retail order flow?
drills.a: Retail flow is uninformed: near-zero adverse selection per fill, so wholesalers internalize profitably (earn spread net of required price improvement) even after paying ~$0.0005-0.0017/share routing fees. The regulatory controversy asks whether the wholesale margin exceeds retail's price improvement - different question from whether individual fills beat NBBO.

drills.q: Markouts show your buys drift UP +8bp at +10min. Good execution or something else?
drills.a: Looks like captured value (paid below subsequent value), BUT verify: could be genuine alpha leaking through execution (strategy works), favorable regime luck, or small-size venue effects that vanish at scale. Re-measure at target participation before concluding the desk earns its keep - impact regime shifts with size (sqrt-law).

drills.q: Flash crash: what breaks first in an Avellaneda-Stoikov quoting model?
drills.a: Stationarity assumptions: cancellation rates explode (liquidity vanishes in ms), arrivals become one-sided, vol jumps beyond calibration - inventory skews calibrated calm quote INTO falling knives and adverse selection hits ~100% of flow. Survivors pre-wire hard inventory caps, auto-widen triggers on short-horizon vol/imbalance, and pull-and-requote circuit breakers.

drills.q: Name the three lines of defense and one deliverable each owns for models.
drills.a: 1st: developers/users - documentation, remediation. 2nd: MRM - independent validation, findings register, approval recommendations. 3rd: internal audit - tests that the MRM PROCESS ran as policy requires.

drills.q: PSI between development and current population = 0.32. What do you do?
drills.a: >0.25 = action band: investigate driver (macro shift vs pipeline bug), freeze promotions riding the shift, recalibrate/redevelop through change control if the shift is real and permanent, tighten compensating controls meanwhile.

drills.q: Challenger beats champion by +0.035 AUC on 800 shadow observations over 3 weeks. Promote?
drills.a: No: sample below ~1,000 minimum, no seasonal cycle covered (3 weeks), significance unproven at that n. Extend shadow period to cover a full cycle, run paired-bootstrap significance, verify guardrail metrics unchanged.

drills.q: Which Whale control failure maps to 'renegotiating limit breaches'?
drills.a: Escalation/limit governance: breaches should force de-risking or documented exceptions with authority; renegotiating them under profit pressure converted a limit system into a suggestion box - a core finding of the Senate report alongside the unvalidated VaR change.

drills.q: A Tier 3 summarizer is being repurposed to draft credit-decision memos. Governance step?
drills.a: Re-tier immediately: customer/decision impact now material -> Tier 1/2 validation before expanded use. Silent scope expansion is misuse risk; approved-use boundaries must change through change control first.

drills.q: Give three concrete signs of validator independence theater in an audit.
drills.a: Validation SLAs shorter than any genuine analysis takes; near-100% approval rates with only Low-severity findings ever issued; validators permanently embedded in delivery squads reporting to the business line they review.

drills.q: Your LLM agent hallucinated a fee amount to 40 customers last month. SR 11-7-style handling?
drills.a: Log as model-risk event with severity + root-cause class (retrieval miss vs reasoning error); check monitoring trend vs tolerance band; apply compensating controls (grounded-output constraints, human review on fee topics); feed incident into eval suite as regression case; report per policy. Hallucination = model-risk event, not just a bug ticket.

drills.q: Why does tiering exist rather than full validation for everything?
drills.a: Validation capacity is finite: GSIBs hold thousands of models, so uniform Tier 1 depth creates multi-year queues where real risk hides in backlog. Concentrate depth by materiality x complexity x novelty; accept lighter periodic review where impact is small and reversible.

drills.q: Two assets, vols 20% and 5%, any correlation. Give ERC weights and the resulting capital tilt.
drills.a: w1 = 5/(20+5) = 0.2 on the 20%-vol asset, w2 = 0.8. Correlation cancels for N=2; each contributes exactly 50% of portfolio variance.

drills.q: Compute beta: Cov(stock, market) = 0.0009 daily, Var(market) = 0.0004 daily.
drills.a: beta = 0.0009/0.0004 = 2.25. High-beta name; CAPM would demand a large premium, but remember the flat-SML anomaly means realized compensation is usually lower than CAPM implies.

drills.q: Why does GMV not need expected returns while tangency does? Show both formulas.
drills.a: GMV w = Sigma^-1 1 /(1'Sigma^-1 1) uses only covariance; tangency w proportional to Sigma^-1(mu - rf) needs mu. Since mu estimates carry SE ~ sigma/sqrt(T), GMV is far more stable out-of-sample.

drills.q: A fund wants ERC at 10% vol using bonds (vol 5%) and stocks (16%). Estimate gross leverage.
drills.a: ERC two-asset mix vol ~6-7% unlevered (dominated by bond weight 76%); to hit 10% needs roughly 10/6.9 ~= 1.4x gross. In practice RP funds run futures/swaps leverage with margin lines sized for vol spikes.

drills.q: Your optimizer outputs +180% in one stock and shorts elsewhere. Diagnose and give three fixes.
drills.a: Classic error maximization / corner solution from near-singular Sigma plus noisy mu. Fixes: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage; long-only with position caps and turnover penalty; Black-Litterman prior so views fight equilibrium only where you have real information.

drills.q: Explain in three sentences why a factor with backtest t = 2.4 deserves skepticism.
drills.a: With hundreds of tested characteristics, multiple testing alone yields many t > 2 by chance; Harvey-Liu-Zhu recommend t > 3 for novel claims. Published premia also decay post-publication due to crowding/arbitrage. Demand out-of-sample, cost-adjusted, capacity-aware evidence before allocating.

drills.q: 2022: SPX total return -18%, Agg -13%. Why did risk parity suffer more than the raw numbers suggest?
drills.a: RP levers the bond sleeve 2-3x to equalize risk, so the worst-ever bond year hit levered; simultaneously correlations flipped positive removing diversification; financing costs spiked as rates rose. Result: category drawdowns ~20-30% vs ~-16% for unlevered 60/40.

drills.q: Write the KKT system that traces the long-short efficient frontier exactly with numpy.
drills.a: Solve [[2Cov, mu, 1],[mu',0,0],[1',0,0]] [w,l1,l2]' = [0, r_target, 1]'. Sweep r_target over [min mu, max mu]; each solve gives one frontier point; filter negatives for the long-only approximation (clipping breaks exact optimality).

drills.q: PM says 'we hold 50/50 stocks and bonds, so our book is balanced.' One-sentence correction?
drills.a: Capital is balanced but risk is not: with 16%/5% vols, equities contribute ~90-95% of variance; balance requires equalizing risk contributions (ERC), which puts most capital in bonds.

drills.q: $5M position, 1.5% daily vol. 99% and 95% parametric VaR?
Scale a 1-day 99% VaR of $200K to 10 days. When is this wrong?
drills.a: $200K x sqrt(10) = ~$632K. Wrong under fat tails/vol clustering: multi-day tails grow faster than sqrt(t) when vol is autocorrelated; use overlapping bootstrap or explicit multi-day simulation for regulatory-grade numbers.

drills.q: 250-day year at 97.5% VaR: how many exceptions expected, and what's the Kupiec verdict if you see 12?
drills.a: Expected 6.25. LR_POF with x=12, T=250, p=0.025 gives LR well above 3.841 -> reject the model at 5%. At 97.5% there is enough signal to catch doubling of the true rate within a couple of years - unlike 99%.

drills.q: Why does ES97.5 punish a short-put book more than VaR99 does?
drills.a: Short puts have extreme negative skew: losses concentrate just past the quantile. VaR99 measures only where the tail starts; ES averages the whole loss region beyond it, so skewness and kurtosis translate directly into higher capital.

drills.q: Your desk's exceptions: 3 in the last year, but all within one fortnight. Pass or fail?
drills.a: Count passes (green zone) but conditionally suspicious: clustering violates iid; Christoffersen independence test likely rejects. Root cause: unconditional window entering a vol shock -> move to GARCH-filtered VaR and report conditional backtests alongside counts.

drills.q: Give the two-digitals subadditivity counterexample numbers.
drills.a: Two independent digitals each lose $100M w.p. 0.7%. Each 99%-VaR = $0 (prob below 1%). Combined P(any loss) = 1-(0.993)^2 = ~1.39% > 1%, so joint 99%-VaR ~ $100M > 0 + 0. Merging books increased measured risk - incoherent.

drills.q: Design a reverse stress test for a regional bank in three steps.
drills.a: 1) Define breach: CET1 < regulatory minimum under stress. 2) Choose shock dimensions (rate rise bp, deposit runoff %, spread widening bp). 3) Solve numerically for minimal combination breaching capital (e.g., +250bp AND 35% uninsured-deposit runoff). Report distance-to-breach as vulnerability magnitude.

drills.q: March 16 2020 vs Aug 5 2024 VIX spikes: what distinguishes them for risk design?
drills.a: Mar 2020: VIX peaked 82.69 amid a sustained regime break - SPX fell ~34% over 23 sessions, correlations broke, liquidity vanished for weeks. Aug 2024: intraday spike above ~60 that mean-reverted in days (carry unwind). First breaks capital math; second breaks intraday/stop-loss logic and leverage cascades. Different instruments need different overlays.

drills.q: An AR(1) has phi=0.95 and innovation sigma=1. What is the variance after 20 steps vs the unconditional variance?
drills.a: RW-like accumulation: Var_n = n*sigma^2 would be 20 if phi=1; for phi=0.95, Var_h = sigma^2*(1-phi^(2h))/(1-phi^2) = (1-0.358)/(0.0975) ~ 6.6, saturating toward unconditional 1/(1-0.9025) ~ 10.3. Mean reversion caps uncertainty.

drills.q: ADF t-stat on a monthly series is -2.4 (constant-only spec). Verdict at 5%?
drills.a: FAIL to reject: -2.4 > -2.86 critical value. Treat as unit-root-suspect. But check power: pair with KPSS (H0 stationarity) and inspect ACF decay before concluding - persistent stationary series routinely produce such values.

drills.q: You difference a trend-stationary series and its acf[1] becomes -0.48 with a fitted MA(1) theta = -0.92. Diagnose.
drills.a: Classic overdifferencing: differencing an already-stationary (around deterministic trend) series induces an artificial MA(1) near the invertibility boundary and inflates variance. Detrend instead of difference, or use d=0 with a trend regressor.

drills.q: ACF decays geometrically; PACF cuts off after lag 3. Propose orders and your first alternative candidates.
drills.a: AR(3). Fit neighbors AR(2)/AR(4) plus ARMA(2,1)-style competitors, choose by AIC/BIC, then verify residuals pass Ljung-Box. Plot signatures propose; information criteria confirm.

drills.q: Estimate the small-sample bias of an AR(1) coefficient with true phi=0.8 from T=50 observations (Hurwicz approximation).
drills.a: Bias ~ -(1+3phi)/T = -(1+2.4)/50 = -0.068. Expected estimate ~0.73 instead of 0.80 - material at short samples; use MLE or bootstrap bias correction.

drills.q: Two independent random-walk price series regressed levels-on-levels give slope t=4.1, R^2=0.94, DW=0.31. Interpret.
drills.a: Textbook spurious regression: DW << R^2 (Granger-Newbold heuristic), huge R^2 from shared trending, t meaningless because statistics diverge under unit-root nulls. Difference both or test cointegration via error-correction modeling; never trade this 'relationship'.

drills.q: For AR(2) phi=(0.6,-0.2), verify stationarity via the triangle inequalities.
drills.a: phi1+phi2=0.4<1 ok; phi2-phi1=-0.8<1 ok; |phi2|=0.2<1 ok. Stationary. Roots of z^2-0.6z+0.2 are complex conjugates (discriminant 0.36-0.8<0): damped pseudo-cycle with period 2*pi/angle.

drills.q: Monthly revenue shows growing amplitude December spikes plus upward drift. Give the transformation sequence and candidate model.
drills.a: log() to stabilize multiplicative seasonality -> ADF/KPSS on logs vs log-diffs -> typically d=1, D=1 at m=12 -> fit airline ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)_12 first; add trading-day/holiday regressors (SARIMAX) if calendar-irregular. Validate against seasonal-naive MASE on a held-out year.

drills.q: Why does Ljung-Box p=0.85 on residuals not prove model adequacy?
drills.a: The same data selected orders minimizing autocorrelation, so residual whiteness is partly guaranteed by construction (post-selection optimism); DF should shrink by p+q. Supplement with out-of-sample walk-forward error, ACF inspection at seasonal lags, and stability checks across windows.

drills.q: GARCH(1,1) with alpha=0.08, beta=0.90, omega=0.002 (daily). Long-run daily vol?
drills.a: Unconditional variance = omega/(1-alpha-beta) = 0.002/0.02 = 0.01, so long-run daily vol = 1% (~15.9% annualized x sqrt(252)). Persistence 0.98 -> shock half-life ~34 days.

drills.q: Why is EWMA lambda=0.94 'GARCH without mean reversion'?
drills.a: EWMA is GARCH(1,1) with omega=0, alpha=1-lam=0.06, beta=lam=0.94: alpha+beta=1 exactly (IGARCH boundary), so variance never reverts to a fixed level - it just exponentially tracks recent shocks. Deliberately simple for overnight VaR; the price is no long-run anchor.

drills.q: Your backtest features use Kalman-SMOOTHED levels over history. What is wrong and how do you fix it?
drills.a: Smoothing uses future data relative to each historical point - leakage. Fix: use FILTERED states (only data <= t), refit variance parameters on expanding/rolling windows ending at t, and verify every feature at time t is computable from data available by t.

drills.q: PM asks why Prophet's 80% intervals missed 40% of last quarter's points. Explain and propose a fix.
drills.a: Prophet default intervals simulate future trend pivots from historical changepoint frequency - a heuristic ignoring parameter/seasonality/residual-autocorrelation uncertainty; under-coverage in volatile regimes is expected. Fix: conformal calibration on rolling one-step residuals (empirical quantiles) or quantile-loss model with empirical coverage monitoring.

drills.q: 10-day VaR from a GARCH with persistence 0.98: what is wrong with multiplying 1-day vol by sqrt(10)?
drills.a: sqrt(t) scaling assumes i.i.d. shocks; persistence 0.98 means elevated vol persists across all 10 days, so true 10-day tail risk exceeds the scaled figure materially. Correct: iterate the variance recursion h steps forward and aggregate scenario returns path-wise (filtered simulation).

drills.q: You have 300 series of 60 observations each for forecasting. Deep nets or classical - and why?
drills.a: Global deep models can work despite short per-series length because they pool across series (300x60 = 18k training windows); N-BEATS-style architectures were built exactly for this regime. Still ship an ETS/state-space challenger and seasonal-naive floor per series; promote only if weighted pinball beats floors consistently out-of-sample.

drills.q: Name two reasons TimesFM zero-shot output should not go straight into a bank's capital process.
drills.a: Interval calibration is not guaranteed (tails undertrained; coverage unverified per domain) and domain shift/microstructure dynamics differ from its web-traffic-heavy pretraining corpus - plus auditability/reproducibility requirements (SR 11-7) demand documented training lineage. Use as ensemble baseline with conformal calibration and human validation before anything capital-relevant.

drills.q: After a crash week your Gaussian-GARCH VaR understates risk. Give three upgrades.
drills.a: (1) Student-t or skewed-t innovations for fat tails; (2) GJR/EGARCH asymmetry so negative shocks feed vol harder; (3) iterate multi-day recursion instead of sqrt-scaling, or blend in realized-vol/HAR estimates if intraday data exists. Also check persistence jumped post-break - refit windows may need shortening.

drills.q: M5 was won by LightGBM with lag features. Does that make deep forecasters pointless?
drills.a: No - it makes them dataset-specific. M5 was tabular retail with rich covariates where GBMs excel; M4's univariate 100k-series setting favored pure neural architecture (N-BEATS). Decision rule: many related series + covariates + cold starts -> global models; tabular feature engineering dominates -> GBMs; single governed series -> ETS/ARIMA/state space.

drills.q: Labels are triple-barrier with max holding 12 bars, average exit 5. What purge width and why?
drills.a: Purge = 12 bars (the MAXIMUM label duration). Any train label whose window can reach the test block contaminates; sizing to the 5-bar average leaks exactly the slow-exit tail where rare-event labels live.

drills.q: You shuffled daily bars within each calendar month before k-fold CV. Leak-free?
drills.a: No - shuffling granularity only changes bandwidth of information flow. Labels spanning months and features persisting across boundaries still leak; serial dependence remains within months too. Use purged walk-forward or CPCV.

drills.q: Backtest: Sharpe 2.2 from daily PnL over 4 years, positions held 20 days. Quick significance check?
drills.a: Overlap deflates iid SE by ~sqrt(20) ~ 4.5x. If quoted t came from iid formula it collapses by that factor - a t~4 claim becomes ~0.9. Recompute with Newey-West lag>=20 or trade-level PnL before believing anything.

drills.q: Your features include a 60-day moving average. How should embargo be sized?
drills.a: By measured memory: the MA's information decays over ~half its window (~30 days); default 1%-of-bars embargo (~10 days on 1000) is too short. Size embargo >= feature ACF half-life so post-test data cannot carry test-period state back into later trains.

drills.q: CSCV reports PBO=0.15 for your search over 40 configs. Does the chosen strategy have alpha?
drills.a: Unknown - PBO=0.15 says your SELECTION process generalizes within this experiment (winner stays above median OOS), not that edge exists. Check DSR for luck-adjusted significance, then costs, capacity, and shadow-trading confirmation.

drills.q: Plain linear regression was trained with full-data-fitted scaler. Redo needed?
drills.a: For unregularized OLS specifically, affine scaling cancels in predictions - numerically harmless. But audit siblings in the pipeline: target encoders, imputation constants, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning on the same full sample are NOT invariant. Fix policy to fit-in-fold regardless of estimator exemptions.

drills.q: Fundamental factors were joined on fiscal-quarter period rather than announcement date. Consequence?
drills.a: Restatement lookahead: historical models see revised numbers weeks/quarters before publication. Inflates value/quality factor backtests systematically. Rebuild joins on actual disclosure timestamps (point-in-time), quantify the delta, and distrust any result computed pre-fix.

drills.q: Name two reasons your limit-order-fill backtest still overstates live performance even after purge/embargo/CPCV all pass.
drills.a: (1) Adverse selection: crossing orders fill disproportionately when you're wrong (informed flow takes the other side). (2) Impact + latency: square-root-law cost of your own size plus drift between signal and arrival; partial fills leave alpha unfilled. Calibrate from execution/TCA data, simulate LOB fills, stress capacity.

drills.q: What belongs in a trial registry and why does undercounting N matter?
drills.a: Every configuration-dataset pair ever evaluated: model families, lookback grids eyeballed, inherited prior research on the signal, abandoned branches. N feeds DSR/multiple-testing corrections - undercounting converts snooped selection into apparent statistical significance; 'we tried 12' usually means 'we remember 12.'

drills.q: Price an AI study-helper: state the three anchors you compute before picking a number.
drills.a: COGS floor (token math x usage skew, P90 user), value ceiling (tutoring hours avoided x loaded rate, or grade-outcome value), market anchor ($30/user enterprise precedent; consumer-chat anchors). Then packaging: hybrid seat~P80 + credits given AI usage variance.

drills.q: Why is 'AI-powered' not a positioning statement?
drills.a: It's a feature adjective every competitor also claims - it names no category, buyer, or alternative. Positioning picks the judge: name the market category, target segment, and unique attributes vs named alternatives (Dunford's chain). 'AI-powered X' ages in months as capability commoditizes.

drills.q: List the six killers and mark which two die most often pre-GA.
drills.a: Undefined outcome, no evals, unit economics, trust/compliance, workflow non-integration, ownership ambiguity. Most pre-GA deaths: undefined outcome + missing evals (pilots can't prove success so they stall) and unit economics discovered late.

drills.q: VP wants Copilot-style $30/user pricing. Construct the response.
drills.a: Explain what $30 encodes (M365 installed base + distribution + workflow embedment), then price YOUR economics: COGS floor incl skew + validated value ceiling + WTP bands; propose sequencing if $30 is already in the board deck - launch with grandfathering language, instrument realized value, revisit at renewal with data.

drills.q: Design credits for a coding-assistant with median 400 req/mo, P95 3,000 req/mo, COGS $0.008/req.
drills.a: Median COGS ~$3.20/mo, P95 ~$24/mo. Seat at ~$19-29 covers through ~P80-P90 allowance (e.g., 1,500 req = $12 included); beyond it, credits at 3-5x marginal (~$0.03/req); hard cap on runaway loops. Most users never see limits; P95 funds itself.

drills.q: Support-AI vendor wants per-resolution pricing. When does this work and when does it explode?
drills.a: Works when resolution is verifiable both sides (closed without reopen within window) and QA sampling exists. Explodes with definition drift ('resolved' disputes), lagged reopenings, buyer-side data quality issues, or multi-causal outcomes. Contract needs: resolution definition, measurement window, dispute mechanism.

drills.q: Bundled AI dropped margins 12 points. Undo the bundle?
drills.a: Usually no - unbundling reads as a pay-cut. Keep bundle, add fair-use limits, migrate heavy users to higher tiers with credits, engineer COGS down (cascade/caching). Announce nothing; fix quietly. The ratchet lesson: bundling AI raises COGS forever against flat pricing power - decide before, not after.

drills.q: Run a Van Westendorp for your tutoring AI: what four questions, what sample, what traps?
drills.a: Too-cheap-to-trust / bargain / expensive-but-considerable / too-expensive. 100+ real buyers per segment (300+ to split), concrete offer description first. Traps: anchoring on consumer chat prices, power-user WTP skewing means, stated-WTP being perception bands not purchase promises - validate with cohort price tests.

drills.q: Your product gets called 'just a wrapper.' What four properties end the accusation?
drills.a: (1) Proprietary data loop with measured outcome improvement; (2) workflow embedment taking months to rebuild; (3) eval/compliance depth in a regulated niche; (4) distribution advantage. If none exist, the label is correct - fix strategy before messaging.

drills.q: Pilot shows great demos but legal review has stalled it for a quarter. Which killer(s) and countermeasures?
drills.a: Killer #4 (trust/compliance), usually compounded by #2 (no evals = nothing to show legal) and #6 (no owner driving). Countermeasures: PII redaction/data-flow diagrams in the design doc, golden-set eval reports as compliance artifacts, human-in-loop escalation paths, audit logging, one named owner running a weekly unblock cadence with legal's requirements converted into testable gates.

drills.q: Rewrite 'Would you use an AI flashcard generator?' into two compliant interview questions.
drills.a: 'Tell me about the last time you made flashcards — walk me through it step by step' (episode) and 'What's the most you've ever done to fix that part of studying?' (workaround/receipts). Past behavior, no embedded solution.

drills.q: Compute the opportunity score: importance 9.1, satisfaction 2.4. And for importance 4.3, satisfaction 6.8?
drills.a: 9.1 x (10-2.4) = 69.2 -> build-worthy target (important AND miserable). 4.3 x (10-6.8) = 13.8 -> kill: unimportant regardless of satisfaction.

drills.q: Your smoke page converts cold traffic at 0.8%. What do you conclude and do?
drills.a: Below the ~1-2% floor, so demand as framed is dead — but check the framing confound first: if a sibling value proposition converted materially better (e.g., 9%), copy/framing was the problem and you pivot to the winner; if all framings fail, kill within a week at ~$200 cost instead of two quarters.

drills.q: Users praise your prototype enthusiastically in every interview but usage after launch is near zero. Explain with the four forces.
drills.a: Praise is pull only. Switching requires push evidenced by workarounds, credible pull, low anxiety, and low habit cost. Habit + anxiety beat polite pull: users stay with painful-but-known tools. Fix by measuring push pre-build (receipts), then reducing anxiety (reversibility, imports, trust signals).

drills.q: Design a 2-week discovery plan for AI hints in a practice tool, with two kill conditions.
drills.a: Days 1-2 telemetry/ticket mining for stuck-signals; days 3-6 six Mom-Test interviews on last stuck-episode; days 7-8 opportunity scoring; days 9-14 Wizard-of-Oz hints manually for 10-15 learners. Kill conditions e.g.: fewer than half report active workarounds; Oz hints don't lift next-attempt success >=15%.

drills.q: A stakeholder wants to survey 500 users instead of 8 interviews. When is each right, in what order?
drills.a: Interviews discover unknown options/mechanisms; surveys size prevalence across KNOWN options. Sequence: interview first to generate the answer space, then survey to size it. A big survey of leading questions industrializes bias.

drills.q: Two distinct solutions under one opportunity both failed their experiments. What now?
drills.a: Prune the opportunity itself: two independent failures suggest the opportunity lacks pull rather than bad execution. Slide up the tree, re-interview around the parent outcome, or reallocate to a higher-scoring sibling branch.

drills.q: How would you detect fabricated episodes from incentive-driven survey-taker recruits?
drills.a: Screen with open-ended past-behavior questions ('walk me through the last time...') where fabricators run out of specifics fast; cross-check dates/tools/details; prefer in-product triggered recruits who verifiably did the behavior recently.

drills.q: An LLM persona panel says 70% of students would adopt your study-buddy. What is this evidence worth?
drills.a: Zero evidentiary weight for validation — synthetic respondents have no causal link to real demand. Its only legitimate use is prioritizing which real interviews to run first or stress-testing question design. Citing it as validation is a red flag.

drills.q: Your team has run discovery for three cycles without shipping anything testable. Diagnose and prescribe.
drills.a: Process has replaced the goal (procrastination-by-process). Prescribe Torres-style cadence guard: weekly touchpoints, a decision artifact every cycle, and force the cheapest ladder test this week; if the tree keeps growing while nothing behavioral gets tested, cap total discovery timebox and require a flagged experiment before more interviews.

drills.q: Compute required n per arm: baseline 5%, detect +10% relative, alpha .05, power .8.
You have 12,000 users/arm and a 5% baseline. What relative MDE can you detect at 80% power?
drills.a: delta = (1.96+0.84) x sqrt(2 x 0.05 x 0.95 / 12000) ~= 0.0158 absolute -> ~31.6% relative MDE. If your plausible lift is +10%, this test is underpowered - don't run it and call the null 'no effect'.

drills.q: Stakeholder wants results by Friday; you get 8K eligible users/day. Respond with numbers.
drills.a: By Friday (~4-5 days) you collect ~32-40K total (~16-20K/arm), buying roughly +-1.9-2.2pt absolute noise floor on a 5% baseline (~38-44% relative MDE) - far above any plausible effect. Show that MDE-vs-deadline table and renegotiate: two weeks buys ~+10% relative.

drills.q: Design the sequential-testing setup for an exec who WILL check daily.
drills.a: Either group-sequential alpha spending with pre-declared looks (day-3/7/14 boundaries where early looks need extreme z-scores like |z|>3+), or anytime-valid mSPRT p-values valid under arbitrary stopping. Policy fix too: dashboard shows sequential-valid stats or hides significance until planned end.

drills.q: Week-1 read shows +18% engagement; week-3 steady state is +7%. Ship decision math?
drills.a: Price against STEADY state (+7%), not peak: maintenance + inference COGS recur monthly, so halving effects often flip NPV negative. Check where the win concentrated (segments), then decide; also note monotone decay predicted shrinkage - the trajectory was the tell.

drills.q: An AI feature costs $60K/mo inference at full rollout. Sketch the experiment plan.
drills.a: Compute break-even uplift first (what gain covers $60K/mo), power the test against THAT as minimum interesting effect; add cost guardrails (tokens/session cap, cost/session target); consider staged rollout to bound learning spend; write the dollar kill-threshold before launch.

drills.q: Referral feature test shows no lift under user-level randomization. What might be wrong?
drills.a: Interference: treated users' referrals change control users' outcomes, diluting estimates toward zero and hiding real network value. Fix: cluster randomization by graph community or geo so spillover stays within arms, accepting higher variance/fewer effective units.

drills.q: 15 concurrent experiments across teams - what infrastructure discipline is mandatory?
drills.a: Layered orthogonal hashing so tests share traffic without colliding; central assignment service with consistent unit IDs; automated SRM/guardrail gates on every dashboard; multiple-comparison policy; decision log linking launches to readouts. Same-surface tests need exclusive layers or explicit factorial interaction analysis.

drills.q: Traffic is 2,000 users/week. Can anything meaningful be A/B tested? Options?
drills.a: At ~4K total over two weeks the detectable relative MDE on a 10% baseline exceeds ~40% - nothing product-relevant fits. Switch instruments: interrupted time series, day-level switchbacks, synthetic control, moderated-test proxy outcomes; or fix traffic itself as the binding constraint on future learning.

drills.q: A teammate proposes dropping confidence from 95% to 80% to ship faster. Legitimate?
drills.a: Legitimate IF pre-declared and priced: consciously accepting more false positives for speed/power. Illegitimate when done post-hoc to make a marginal result significant - that's peeking with extra steps. Write the error-budget tradeoff into the plan before results exist.

drills.q: Write the skeleton of an ask paragraph: what six elements?
drills.a: Decision + resource + duration + deadline + default-if-silent + what-no-means. Example: 'Approve 1 engineer and $3K/mo inference for 6 weeks to validate AI hints against our eval gate; decide by Friday; silence = no; a no costs a quarter of learning and we revisit with vendor data.'

drills.q: Name the eight blocks of a fundable one-pager in order.
drills.a: Decision requested (size/deadline/default) -> problem+why-now -> evidence (2-3 sourced numbers) -> cheapest path -> value band vs cost band -> alternatives incl. do-nothing -> top-3 risks x mitigations -> kill condition. ~450-600 words.

drills.q: Your value model: low $150K, mid $400K, high $800K/yr; cost $315K. How do you frame the ask?
drills.a: Tranche it: ~3 x $105K with re-up gates ('evidence >= X% of midpoint before tranche two'), payback ~9.5 months at midpoint, and show whether the case survives pessimistic-value x doubled-cost. '$105K buys the next proof point; stop-loss defined' beats one faith-based ask.

drills.q: CFO challenges your churn assumption mid-meeting. Walk the live response.
drills.a: Don't defend - recompute together on their input; state whether the decision flips. Survives: 'even at your churn we clear cost.' Doesn't: 'your churn is exactly why tranche-one gates exist - we learn cheaply before most spend.' If you can't recompute live, commit to the sensitivity table within 24-48h and deliver.

drills.q: Sequence the pre-alignment work for a controversial platform consolidation.
drills.a: Stakeholder map -> socialize problem statement in 1:1s incorporating feedback visibly -> skeptic preview ('what would kill this?') -> their objection answered IN doc with credit -> final >=48h ahead, comments open -> meeting on unresolved threads only -> explicit decision/owner/date. Roughly 60% of influence happens before anyone sees the doc.

drills.q: 'Great doc, wrong quarter.' What do you do in the next 48 hours?
drills.a: Ask 'what would need to be true for Q2?'; classify capacity vs priority vs slow-no; shrink tranche to fit discretionary space or attach to blocker's metric; set dated follow-up; ship cheapest unblockable slice generating evidence so next cycle arrives with data instead of the same slide.

drills.q: Your funded project missed its promised band. What do you send leadership?
drills.a: Actuals-vs-promise report within the quarter, unprompted: which assumption failed, what was learned, remaining runway decision recommendation (kill per pre-registered condition or pivot). Honest misses compound credibility fastest; defending zombies burns budget AND reputation.

drills.q: Write for executives who give docs 90 seconds: five mechanics plus the test.
drills.a: Ask+stakes inside 50 words; one-screen self-sufficiency; assertion-headings carrying conclusions; numbers as tables; hedges killed. Test: hand to an outsider for 90 seconds - can they state ask/stakes/deadline? Failure means revise, not explain.

drills.q: A peer agrees in 1:1s then torpedoes your proposals publicly. Full playbook.
drills.a: Verify pattern (minutes); take objections seriously enough to write down; circulate earlier with written-dissent deadlines; in-meeting redirect: 'that's addressed page two - which test does the mitigation fail?'; one direct private relationship conversation if persistent; escalation reserved for genuine bad faith. Going around them converts a peer into an enemy with receipts.

drills.q: When is acting WITHOUT a document the right call?
drills.a: Reversible two-way-door decisions inside your authority (experiment flags, bounded tooling trials): act, document outcomes after. Emergencies invert the pipeline. Boundary test: state which door you're walking through BEFORE walking through it - decisiveness is acting inside mandate and reporting; process-violation is acting outside mandate regardless of outcome quality.

drills.q: Pick and defend a North Star for a tutoring platform.
drills.a: Weekly active learners completing an assessed activity (value received, sum-form, plausible renewal link). Reject logins (activity), courses completed (quantity-gaming), DAU/MAU (ratio). Close with cohort validation that high-NS quarters preceded higher renewal.

drills.q: Write two guardrail thresholds for a ranking-model change.
drills.a: E.g., p95 latency <= baseline + 10%; relevance score >= -1% vs control; complaint/flag rate <0.5% of sessions; next-7-day return non-negative within noise. Thresholds set from historical variance, signed off BEFORE results exist.

drills.q: Compute downstream impact: activation moves 28% -> 34%. Relative lift on everything after?
drills.a: 6pts / 28% ~= 21.4% relative increase in activated users, multiplying every later stage's volume proportionally. That leverage is why activation usually beats retention polish when the retention curve already flattens.

drills.q: Build the metric tree for an enterprise LMS (Cornerstone-style) with renewal-revenue outcome.
drills.a: NS: weekly active learners completing >=1 assessed activity. Inputs: new-seat activation <=7 days, manager-assigned coverage, median weekly minutes/active learner, W8 return rate. Guardrails: course-quality rating >=4.0/5, compliance-deadline miss rate falling, tickets per 1K learners. Each input gets SQL-exact definition to kill definition disputes.

drills.q: Growth wants signups; infra wants cost/user down. Resolve without seniority.
drills.a: Escalate to shared parent units: marginal NS value per signup (cohort LTV by channel) vs cost per user; set a written exchange rate in planning - accept paid signups while CAC payback <=12 months and gross margin >=75%. Conflicting local optima are normal; resolving by unwritten vibes is not.

drills.q: Month one of a new AI tutoring feature: what do you instrument, what do you defer?
drills.a: Instrument only: outcome (% hint-sessions ending in independent correct solution <24h), inputs (hint-request rate, post-hint success), guardrails (over-reliance flag >70% hint-attempts, token cost/session), weekly cohort readout. Defer NPS/referral/trees until behavior stabilizes ~week 6-8. Attention bandwidth is the constraint, not storage.

drills.q: Design a Goodhart stress test for 'minutes practiced' as headline.
drills.a: Ask how the number could rise while reality doesn't: idle-session stuffing, autoplay grinding, repeat-easy-content farming. Attach counter-metrics (checkpoint pass rate, next-day return, content diversity floor) and run net arithmetic: headline gain minus weighted guardrail losses; if net ~0 it's grind, iterate rather than celebrate.

drills.q: Post-iOS14.5, why distrust channel-level ROI dashboards and what replaces them?
drills.a: Identifier loss makes last-click attribution systematically wrong and walled gardens double-count conversions. Replace with incrementality testing (geo holdouts, conversion-lift studies) plus first-party behavioral proxies; treat platform-reported ROAS as directional and say so in writing.

drills.q: Execs want one number on the dashboard. What goes up and what must accompany it?
drills.a: One output-form NS + 2-3 inputs + 1-2 guardrails as sparklines vs targets, with mandatory anomaly annotation within a day and a two-click drill-down (NS -> inputs -> segments/experiments) built before accepting the slot - owning the question chain keeps the number yours.

drills.q: A marketplace has supply-side and demand-side health pulling apart. One North Star?
drills.a: Prefer TWO explicit stars balanced deliberately (e.g., bookings AND host earnings) over one number pretending the tension away - forcing one invites optimizing the easier side into imbalance. If leadership insists on one, use a bounded composite with publicly agreed weights and monitor both components separately for divergence.

drills.q: A VP says 'build AI summaries in the dashboard.' Give the two questions you ask before any architecture discussion.
drills.a: 'What user behavior would tell us this worked?' (outcome) and 'What problem does that outcome imply — who hurts today, how often, at what cost?' (problem). You're walking UP the chain from their solution before evaluating it.

drills.q: Rewrite this as an outcome: 'Ship report summaries by end of Q3 with 95% coverage.'
drills.a: Something like: 'Raise report-follow-through (reports leading to an export/share/action within 48h) from 12% to 18% within two quarters, without degrading p95 load time beyond +100ms.' Behavior + baseline + magnitude + timeframe + guardrail.

drills.q: Compute the annual COGS of an AI feature: 5M requests/month, 1,500 tokens/request, $3 per million tokens.
drills.a: 5e6 x 1500 = 7.5B tokens/mo = 7,500 Mtok x $3 = $22.5K/mo = $270K/yr. The feature must plausibly move >$270K/yr of value to clear its own floor.

drills.q: Your recsys gave +25% engaged interactions. List the full translation chain to revenue and label each link's confidence.
drills.a: +25% interactions -> +20% session length (measured, high confidence) -> +5pts D7 return rate (cohort correlation, medium) -> ARPU via LTV model ($0.31/D7 pt/mo, modeled, weakest link) -> 5pts x $0.31 x 4.2M MAU ~= $6.5M/mo face; present a $4-8M/yr band.

drills.q: A proposal's best case is $300K/yr and needs 2 engineers for 2 quarters plus inference spend. What do you do?
drills.a: Build the one-page ledger: fully loaded opportunity cost ~$400-600K exceeds best-case value even before run-cost. Present arithmetic, not opinion, plus a cheap probe whose result would have to be wildly positive to change the math — and let the review conclude 'not yet'.

drills.q: Write the kill condition for an AI study-buddy feature in a tutoring app.
drills.a: Example: 'If after 4 weeks fewer than 15% of new sessions include a study-buddy interaction, or follow-through-to-next-action doesn't rise >=2pts vs matched cohorts, we cut it.' Specific threshold + timeframe + cheaply observable metric, written before build start.

drills.q: Sales promised a customer a bespoke feature that would create a money-losing one-off architecture. Walk your response.
drills.a: First extract the job the customer is hiring the feature for; check for a cheaper path solving the same need. If the custom work is structurally bad, put lifetime numbers side by side in writing and reframe as pricing: take it as paid professional services or negotiate reference rights so the loss is deliberate and capped.

drills.q: Feature shipped on time, adoption fine, target metric flat. Diagnose in order.
drills.a: (1) Adoption without behavior change — check depth-of-use not activation; (2) outcome dominated by other drivers — segment; affected cohort may have moved 20% but be 4% of base; (3) the original theory linking feature to outcome was wrong. Cohort cuts before theory. Then re-price ongoing cost against the smaller-than-hoped benefit.

drills.q: Translate p95 latency -400ms on a checkout flow into dollars, stating your assumptions.
drills.a: Use a fitted elasticity, not folklore: assume ~0.5% conversion per 100ms (conservative vs commonly cited 1%/100ms figures). On $40M/yr checkout GMV: 4 units of 100ms x 0.5% = ~2% relative... applied conservatively as 2% of $40M ~= $800K/yr, banded and labeled modeled-until-fitted-on-our-own-funnel-data.

drills.q: Three candidate projects, one quarter. Describe the selection artifact you build and the tie-breaker.
drills.a: One page each: problem statement, outcome + baseline, three solution candidates, cheapest path to evidence, kill condition, value-per-week arithmetic. Compare expected annualized value band vs weeks-to-first-evidence. On value ties prefer optionality/reversibility — failure leaves reusable infra, success doesn't lock the roadmap.

drills.q: Name the five forces and one AI-era example of each.
drills.a: Supplier: model API vendor controls COGS. Buyer: enterprise contracts vs zero-switching consumers. Substitutes: users reading the doc themselves instead of your summaries. Entrants: funded team cloning in <8 weeks. Rivalry: five competitors shipping near-identical features on the same base models.

drills.q: Run the attacker test on 'our chatbot is better because we fine-tuned.'
drills.a: Fails unless training data is structurally scarce: a funded competitor replicates fine-tuning in weeks if data is scrapeable/synthetic-replaceable. Passes only with hard-to-replicate data feeding a real improvement loop (e.g., years of per-student mastery traces).

drills.q: Compute: build = 3 eng-months + $6.5K/mo run; vendor = $2.4K/mo, exit 1 eng-month. 3-year horizon at $30K/eng-month loaded.
drills.a: Build: 3 x ~$120K (at $30K/mo... using 160h x rate) + run 6.5K x 36 = roughly $360K+234K = ~$594K. Buy: 2.4K x 36 = $86K + exit ~$120K = ~$206K. BUY - commodity component, cheap exit, no moat contribution.

drills.q: Draw a mini Wardley map for a RAG product; identify one play.
drills.a: Need: trusted answers from private docs. Chain: chat UI (product) -> orchestration (custom->product fast) -> retrieval (commodity-ish) -> embeddings (utility) -> generation (utility). Plays: open-source the orchestrator to commoditize competitors' chains while differentiating on eval harness; or compliance-wrapped deployment exploiting enterprise inertia.

drills.q: CEO fears '[Cloud Giant] will clone us.' Give the serious assessment checklist.
drills.a: Distribution? Data loop (years of usage traces)? Workflow embedment/migration friction for installed users? Incentive (market big enough AND non-cannibalizing)? Track record of maintaining keynote categories after 18 months? Score honestly: real risk -> differentiate into workflow/trust layers now; noise -> stop relitigating.

drills.q: Should a mid-size company self-host open-weight models? The economics.
drills.a: Usually no below scale: serving engineering + GPU ops ~= several engineers fully loaded (~$1M+/yr) versus API prices falling ~10x per 18-24 months (drift against you). Cross-over cases: extreme privacy constraints, predictable giant volume, latency-critical edge inference.

drills.q: Vendor announces 5x price increase on a core dependency. Playbook?
drills.a: Quantify COGS exposure in unit-economics terms; invoke contract terms; negotiate with credible alternative as leverage; activate pre-priced exit plan (abstraction layer = weeks not quarters); then log into ledger process - diversify where cheap via dual-provider interfaces, accept where switching costs exceed expected repeat-shock losses.

drills.q: Your product's users start scripting against internal endpoints. Platform now?
drills.a: Not yet automatically: verify pull evidence volume (unsolicited integrations, partner inquiries), test toll enforceability (metering/billing/ToS), accept platform tax consciously (compat forever, slower iteration). Without builder density ship product-with-clean-API plus private partner integrations; formalize when partners outnumber your own roadmap items.

drills.q: New AI-compliance obligations land 2026-2027. Threat or opportunity for an incumbent? A challenger?
drills.a: Incumbent: opportunity disguised as burden - costs amortize across revenue, raising entry barriers around installed base. Challenger: compliance-forward positioning in risk-sensitive segments (health/finance/education) where buyers pay premiums for certified boringness. Both: build evidence pipelines once (eval logs, docs, incident response) as reusable moat input.

drills.q: 'Our AI assistant began as a feature - when does it deserve business-level investment?'
drills.a: When it shows independent retention (users return specifically for it), standalone-attributable unit economics (own activation funnel, measurable willingness-to-pay), and a defensible wedge. Until then it borrows the parent's moat and shouldn't pay business-team prices - funding it as one creates an orphaned team that neither moves the host nor survives alone.

drills.q: Compute LTV: $29 ARPU, 68% gross margin, 4%/mo churn.
drills.a: Lifetime = 1/0.04 = 25 months; LTV = 29 x 0.68 x 25 ~= $493. With CAC of $150 that's LTV:CAC ~= 3.3x (passes the >=3 heuristic) and payback = 150/(29x0.68) ~= 7.6 months.

drills.q: Cost per request: 800 input + 400 output tokens, $0.25/Mtok in, $1/Mtok out (small model).
drills.a: 800/1e6 x $0.25 = $0.0002; 400/1e6 x $1 = $0.0004; total $0.0006/request - ~21x cheaper than the frontier example ($0.0126). This ratio is what makes cascades transformative.

drills.q: Why is comparing paid-channel CAC against blended LTV self-deception?
drills.a: Blended LTV includes organic/referred users who cost little to acquire and often retain better; pairing it with paid CAC makes paid channels look far healthier than they are. Compare paid CAC against paid-cohort LTV, or compare both on a blended basis - consistently.

drills.q: Build the unit economics: AI feature, $29 seat, 25% free users, median 8 req/wk x2 skew, $0.0126/req, plus $2.10 support+hosting/user/mo.
drills.a: Token COGS mean = 8 x 4.33 x 0.0126 x 2 ~= $0.87; total COGS ~$2.97/user/mo. Blended ARPU = 29 x 0.75 = $21.75. Gross profit ~$18.8 -> GM ~86% blended... but recompute free-rider share of COGS carefully: if free users consume equally, paying users carry their COGS too - sensitivity table mandatory.

drills.q: Design usage-based pricing protecting margin for an AI tutoring assistant.
drills.a: Seat priced off median-user COGS at target GM covering ~P80 usage; metered credits beyond allowance at 3-5x marginal COGS (support/variance/free-rider subsidy); hard caps or degressive pricing on agent-style loops; cheap pricing for cached/batch paths to shape demand. Model the distribution, not the average.

drills.q: Business case for 2 quarters cutting inference cost 40%: walk it and say when you'd reject your own project.
drills.a: Current annualized COGS x 40% = recurring savings vs eng cost $400-800K; express payback months + 3yr NPV; add strategic kicker (enables free tier/pricing moves). If current spend is only ~$300K/yr, reject: propose caching config instead. Showing when NOT to do your own project is credibility gold.

drills.q: Your eval sweep shows mid-tier model within 3pts of frontier at 8x lower cost, but 2% of cases fail badly. Architecture?
drills.a: Cascade with confidence routing: mid-tier answers most traffic; uncertain/low-confidence cases escalate to frontier. You buy frontier quality exactly where failures concentrate while paying commodity prices elsewhere - typically recovers most of the gap at a fraction of full-frontier cost.

drills.q: Cohort analysis reveals new-channel acquisitions retain half as long. Actions?
drills.a: Recompute cohort/channel-level LTV and payback; pause channels whose cohort-LTV < CAC despite okay blends; adjust targeting toward retained-profile lookalikes; write falsifiable 'retention improves with maturity' bets with mechanisms and checkpoints if leadership wants to continue - hope isn't a mechanism.

drills.q: An agent product burns 50x single-shot tokens per task. Options?
drills.a: (1) Price like labor - reposition competitor set from software to people; (2) engineer token intensity: aggressive context management, small-model substeps, caching of tool outputs; (3) restrict agent loops with budgets/caps; (4) charge per outcome/task not per seat so COGS scales with willingness-to-pay. Unmanaged, 50x burn destroys any seat-price model.

drills.q: Finance challenges your engagement-uplift value claim. What do you bring?
drills.a: The full chain with confidence labels ($4-8M/yr band from module-01 method) PLUS the incremental serving bill from measured compute deltas, netted into margin impact, with a sensitivity table (engagement halved, compute doubled still clears zero). Volunteering both sides preempts silent re-derivation and buys credibility for future claims.

drills.q: Name the eight labs defining the 2026 frontier and one structural fact about how families ship.
drills.a: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI (closed-first); DeepSeek, Qwen/Alibaba, Mistral, Meta (open-weight/transition). Structural: every family ships a tier ladder â€” flagship/workhorse/fast â€” spanning ~$1.25-$50/M output tokens, with reasoning-effort dials and ~1M-token contexts.

drills.q: List the five model-card audit lenses from memory.
drills.a: EVALS (cited vs omitted, vendor vs independent, tier, precision), DATA (sources, cutoff, contamination method), LICENSE (OSI status, thresholds, carve-outs, incorporated policies, output rights), SAFETY (red-team scope + residual-risk owner), OPERATIONS (pinning, static notices, output ceilings, emissions).

drills.q: A teammate calls a Llama-class model 'open source.' Correct them precisely.
drills.a: It's open-weight, not open source: the Community License fails OSI's definition per OSI's own analysis â€” purpose restrictions via AUP, user-class discrimination (700M MAU provision), field-of-endeavor limits, EU carve-outs in some versions. MIT/Apache 2.0 convey actual open-source freedoms; community licenses convey revocable privileges with silent-update risk.

drills.q: Quote three contamination statistics that justify distrusting raw public benchmark numbers.
drills.a: ~29.1% of MMLU items flagged contaminated (JHU NAACL 2024); C-Eval ~45.8%; multilingual benchmarks up to ~91.8%. Supporting: Meta self-reported 16% MMLU overlap for Llama 2; GPT-4 report admitted 9/34 exams >20% overlap; clean mirrors drop GSM8K ~13 points; ITD removes ~22.9% of MMLU inflation.

drills.q: Why do n-gram decontamination filters miss leaks, and what actually works?
drills.a: Exact-match filters (13-gram GPT-3 era, 40-gram GPT-4) can't catch paraphrases, translations, or reformatted tables â€” the dominant multilingual leak path (~92% contamination). Works better: dynamic benchmarks refreshed from post-cutoff sources (LiveBench), private held-out sets (MMLU-CF), and inference-time decontamination.

drills.q: A card shows great scores but you'll deploy int8 quantization. What's the issue and the fix?
drills.a: The bf16-vs-deployed precision gap: Llama 4's card explicitly evaluates on bf16 while shipping quantized checkpoints â€” published numbers don't describe your artifact. Fix: demand precision-matched evaluations from the vendor or run your own quantized-model eval on your private set before committing the serving configuration.

drills.q: Your product serves EU users. Which license lens items fire during teardown?
drills.a: Jurisdictional carve-outs first â€” certain Llama license versions explicitly restricted EU-based users; then AUP incorporated-by-reference (updatable terms), attribution mechanics for distribution pipelines, and data-provenance disclosures mapping to GDPR duties. This is exactly why license review gates pilots rather than launches.

drills.q: Mid-2026 saw a flagship suspended 22 days by export controls and another gated 12 days for government review. What do you change Monday morning?
drills.a: Treat regulatory state as an availability dimension: test (not merely document) multi-vendor fallback quarterly, keep the abstraction layer, wire regulatory monitoring into ops alerting, pin snapshot IDs with rotation diffs, and allocate suspension risk in vendor contracts. The trigger is policy; the blast radius is engineering readiness.

drills.q: Vendor reports SOTA but discloses no contamination methodology and no independent reproductions. Walk your assessment.
drills.a: Treat numbers as unverified upper bounds: check third-party indexes (disclosure ranges 8/8 down to 0/8 across majors), run private task evals, consult dynamic-benchmark standings, ask the vendor directly for filter sizes and overlap stats. Silence where peers disclose is itself decision-relevant disclosure-quality information.

drills.q: Contrast DeepSeek vs Meta openness strategies and extract the durable lesson.
drills.a: DeepSeek: consistent MIT licensing of frontier MoE flagships + R-reasoners with published recipes â€” openness as strategy that reset pricing globally. Meta: openness as instrument â€” Llama under a non-OSI Community License seeded an ecosystem, then frontier pivoted closed before partial Apache reopenings. Durable lesson: openness is a per-model LICENSE property, not a lab identity; audit every model, trust no lineage.

drills.q: CFO asks why comparable-capability models vary ~40x in price. Answer without hand-waving.
drills.a: Positioning margin vs volume tiers; inference structure (MoE active params, reasoning-token burn at effort tiers); bundling of managed safety/SLAs/compliance; strategic anchoring â€” MIT competitors floor pricing near $1.25/M while capability-at-any-price buyers sustain $50/M premiums; market immaturity means price moves faster than value evidence. Decision rule: price-per-task at your quality bar from your private eval.

drills.q: What map-redraw signals should trigger a portfolio review?
drills.a: Simultaneous multi-lab flagship releases within a month (repricing follows); any lab changing disclosure patterns (strategy shifts precede products); suspension/gating/regulatory events; license-family changes within a lineage; and quarterly incumbent-vs-challenger drift on YOUR private eval even absent external events.

drills.q: Define test-time compute in one sentence and name the two scaling axes it joined.
drills.a: Spending more inference-time compute per query (long internal reasoning chains) to buy accuracy — joining parameters+data (pretraining) and alignment/fine-tuning (post-training) as the third axis. Accuracy improves roughly logarithmically with thinking tokens.

drills.q: What reward signal does RL-on-chains use, and what behaviors emerge from it?
drills.a: Outcome rewards: the final answer is scored against a verifier (unit tests, exact-match, rubrics), and the policy is updated toward chains that produced correct answers. Emergent behaviors: longer chains on hard problems, backtracking ('wait, that's wrong'), re-derivation, approach-switching — reinforced because they correlate with success, not because scripted.

drills.q: Quote the AIME 2024 gap between non-reasoning and reasoning models, plus R1's number.
drills.a: GPT-4o-class ~13% vs o3-class ~96%; DeepSeek-R1 at 79.8% — an open-weight MIT-licensed model at roughly 5% of o1's API price. Also useful: GPQA-Diamond o3 87.7% / R1 71.5%.

drills.q: Why does a reasoning-model invoice look output-dominated when the visible answer is short?
drills.a: Hidden thinking tokens are billed as output: a typical query might be ~500 input tokens against ~5,000 output tokens of which ~4,500 are internal thinking. Hard problems scale to ~50k thinking tokens (~$0.40 o3-class) and hardest tiers to ~57M tokens/~14 min per question. Per-query cost becomes a distribution requiring budget tables and p95 alerting.

drills.q: Sketch the shape of the accuracy-vs-thinking-budget curve and its three corollaries.
drills.a: Logarithmic rise then plateau (sometimes degradation via overthinking loops). Corollaries: saturation points differ per task class (easy saturates in hundreds of tokens; unsolvable never rises); it composes with best-of-k/self-consistency at multiplicative cost; log-shape means budgets are marginal-return decisions, which is why APIs expose coarse effort tiers rather than raw token counts.

drills.q: Name four workload classes where a fast model beats a reasoner even at equal quality, with the mechanism.
drills.a: Chat (latency destroys UX); content generation (style bottleneck — indistinguishable outputs); simple lookups (nothing to compute); orchestration-bound agent loops (wall-clock dominated by tool calls/parsing so thinking premium is wasted); plus subjective/creative work. Mechanism in all: no accuracy gain to offset latency/cost penalties.

drills.q: Design the routing layer for a production assistant: what gets escalated and how do you handle runaway chains?
drills.a: Fast model default (~90% of traffic); escalate on low confidence (logprob/self-consistency signals), hard task classes, or explicit user request; reasoning-as-critic for drafts on critical paths. Runaway handling: token/time ceilings, n-gram repetition loop detectors, fallback to fast model with honest uncertainty signaling, per-task-class budget tables with p95 cost alerting since per-query cost is a distribution.

drills.q: Why can't you treat R1's visible <think> trace as an auditable causal record?
drills.a: Faithfulness gap: RL shapes chains statistically toward rewarded outcomes, so the displayed trace may rationalize a decision rather than reveal its actual causes. Visibility aids debugging and distillation but legibility ≠ faithfulness; compliance-critical flows need outcome-level verification and independent checks instead of chain-inspection certificates.

drills.q: A stakeholder says 'reasoning models solved hallucination.' Give the precise correction.
drills.a: They reduce manipulation-errors (multi-step arithmetic/logic where computation was the failure mode) but fabrication-tendency on missing knowledge persists — a reasoner constructs internally-consistent arguments from false premises fluently. What helps: retrieval grounding, citations, external verifiers, calibrated abstention, self-consistency. Diagnose your error regime before prescribing reasoning as medicine.

drills.q: Your agent spends 45s per action because every step calls a reasoner. Give the restructure plan and expected outcome.
drills.a: Profile steps into thinking-bound vs orchestration-bound; fast model executes routine steps; reserve reasoner for initial planning, critic-verification of consequential actions, and low-confidence recovery; add streaming status UX, parallel tool calls, cached context, per-step-type budget caps. Expected: reasoner touches ~10-20% of steps while task success holds — value comes from matching compute to step difficulty.

drills.q: R1's training recipe became public — does that make frontier reasoning cheap to produce? Distinguish carefully.
drills.a: No — it makes the RECIPE replicable and serving cheap (open weights, ~5% API pricing, distills). Training still consumed serious compute. The disruption was transparency and price pressure plus an open ecosystem; conflating serving cost with training cost is the classic error when citing R1 as 'reasoning is free now.'

drills.q: If inference efficiency improves 100x next year, does hybrid routing become obsolete? Argue both sides briefly.
drills.a: Obsolescence case: cheap-enough thinking removes the cost penalty from escalation. Counter-case: routing optimizes value-to-cost at the margin and cheap reasoning invites broader deployment where trivial-query waste multiplies too (Jevons dynamics); latency still matters regardless of price, and easy queries gain zero accuracy from any budget. Verdict: routing survives as policy even as thresholds move — build it configurable.

drills.q: In one sentence each: what do the backbone, objective, and distillation axes control in generative media?
drills.a: Backbone (U-Net vs DiT): how well quality scales with compute and how flexibly modalities fit in. Objective (epsilon-prediction vs flow matching): path geometry, step requirements, determinism, likelihood. Distillation (LCM/Turbo/PFM): how few sampling steps you can afford and what quality tax they carry.

drills.q: Quote DiT-XL/2's headline numbers versus ADM-U.
drills.a: FID 2.27 on ImageNet 256x256 at 119 Gflops/sample vs ADM-U's 742 Gflops for worse results; at 512x512, FID 3.04 at 525 Gflops vs ADM-U's 3.85 at 2,813 — roughly 5x the compute efficiency.

drills.q: Write the CFM loss used in flow matching.
drills.a: MSE between the network's velocity prediction v(x_t,t) and the constant target x1-x0, where x_t=(1-t)x0+t*x1 is the linear interpolation of noise x0 and data x1. Lipman et al. showed this regression's gradient equals the intractable marginal-flow objective's.

drills.q: A teammate doubles denoising steps from 25 to 50 expecting better outputs. What does the DiT evidence say?
drills.a: Be skeptical: DiT showed model compute beats sampling compute — L/2 at 1000 steps (80.7 Tflops/image) LOST to XL/2 at 128 steps (15.2 Tflops), FID 23.7 vs 25.9. Extra steps can't fix a backbone-limited model; they reliably double inference cost. If quality plateaus, change backbone/data, not the sampler count.

drills.q: If interpolation paths are straight lines, why doesn't one Euler step sample exactly? And what fixes it?
drills.a: Because the marginal velocity field averages over all couplings through a point and is generally nonlinear even though each conditional path is linear; independent pairings create crossing curves. Rectified flow fixes it by re-pairing samples through the trained model and retraining — about two rounds make trajectories nearly straight enough for one-step Euler sampling.

drills.q: Explain why one-step consistency students produce blurry rather than noisy images, and how PFM addresses it.
drills.a: Coarse integration turns the regression into predicting a conditional expectation whose minimizer averages modes — soft blends instead of crisp picks (mean-seeking). PFM supervises decoded predictions in a pretrained perceptual feature space, shifting the minimizer toward mode-seeking, enabling sharp 4-8 step flow generation without any teacher model.

drills.q: You must cut video-generation cost ~5x without changing vendors. Rank the levers and their costs.
drills.a: 1) Distilled checkpoints (50 to 4-8 steps, ~6x measured, quality tax below 4 steps); 2) duration/resolution ladders with draft-then-refine (tokens scale with frames x area); 3) stronger temporal VAE compression; 4) batching/caching/off-peak scheduling. Keep a >=4-step floor because subjective quality collapses visibly beneath it.

drills.q: Outputs look burnt and oversaturated after switching to a guidance-distilled checkpoint. Diagnosis and fix?
drills.a: Classic excessive-guidance signature: CFG pushes samples off-manifold. In a distilled model guidance is baked in (e.g., frozen w=9.0), so there's no live knob — lower guidance if available, otherwise switch checkpoints/tiers rather than hunting for a dial that no longer exists.

drills.q: Where does Sora's spacetime patch idea fit the DiT story, and what breaks first as videos get longer?
drills.a: Spacetime patches are the video entry point: latent spatiotemporal cubes become tokens so the same ViT-style DiT scales across resolutions/durations — no per-format architectures. As length grows, quadratic attention over exploding token counts breaks first, plus temporal-consistency/world-model failures (object permanence), motivating sparse/MoE/linear attention and hierarchical approaches.

drills.q: Your team wants to fine-tune a generator on 5k domain images: DiT or U-Net? Defend briefly.
drills.a: At 5k images scaling-law advantages are irrelevant — transfer decides it: fine-tune whichever pretrained family matches your domain, license, and tooling; both ecosystems are mature. The U-Net-vs-DiT war matters at pretraining scale, not fine-tuning scale; claiming otherwise misapplies frontier-scale evidence to small-data regimes.

drills.q: What evidence would convince you one-step generation has truly matched multi-step quality?
drills.a: A method matching teacher distributions on diversity/tail-fidelity metrics (not headline FID alone) at one-two steps, demonstrated at video scale where temporal coherence compounds per-frame averaging failures. PFM itself admits degradation below two steps — structural mode-seeking loss isn't yet solved, only relocated.

drills.q: Name three things that break in production video pipelines that image pipelines never face.
drills.a: Temporal artifacts (flicker, object-permanence errors across frames), cost explosion from token counts growing linearly with frames (steps x tokens economics), and character/identity consistency across shots requiring reference conditioning or seed discipline. Plus prompt drift over long durations.

drills.q: State the three perceptual latency thresholds for voice agents and the human behavior that sets them.
drills.a: ~200ms is the natural human turn-taking gap; under ~800ms a reply feels responsive/natural; past ~800ms pauses become noticeable; past ~1500ms conversation breaks down â€” users repeat themselves, talk over the agent, or assume the line dropped.

drills.q: List the six stages of a cascaded voice round trip with typical budgets.
drills.a: Uplink+jitter 50-100ms; endpointing 100-500ms; STT partial <250ms; LLM first token 100-600ms; TTS first audio 90-313ms; network hops 50-200ms per vendor leg.

drills.q: What's the difference between VAD and endpointing, in one sentence each?
drills.a: VAD: classifies a single ~20-30ms audio frame as speech or non-speech. Endpointing: decides whether the caller's entire turn has ended and the agent should respond â€” consuming VAD output plus transcript finality plus semantics as inputs.

drills.q: Your agent both interrupts users AND leaves long dead-air pauses. Why won't another silence-threshold pass fix it, and what will?
drills.a: The two complaints pull opposite directions on the same knob, proving silence duration carries no hesitation-vs-completion information. The fix is a semantic layer: score utterance completeness from lexical/syntactic/prosodic content (semantic_vad-style eagerness or a turn-detection model), keeping acoustic VAD for mic gating/noise rejection.

drills.q: Walk through the barge-in loop with its deadline, and name the prerequisite that stops self-interruption.
drills.a: Detect user speech during playback â†’ stop agent audio within ~150ms â†’ flush TTS buffer + queued audio â†’ cancel in-flight LLM generation â†’ reroute new audio to STT. Prerequisite: acoustic echo cancellation, else TTS leaking through the speakerphone mic registers as user speech and the agent barges in on itself.

drills.q: Why is LLM total generation time irrelevant to voice responsiveness, and what metric replaces it?
drills.a: Audio plays while tokens continue streaming, so total generation hides under playback; only time-to-first-token gates responsiveness because chunking and TTS can't start before it. Reduce via fast model tier (100-200 vs 250-600ms), prompt caching, regional colocation, and speaking filler during tool calls.

drills.q: Compare cascaded and speech-to-speech stacks on auditability, model choice, latency, and cost.
drills.a: Cascaded: ground-truth per-stage transcripts (debuggable), any model including fine-tunes, VPC-resident, $0.0095-$0.17/min predictable; ~1400ms sequential â†’ 500-700ms streamed. S2S: ~600-900ms end-to-end, native prosody and interruption, but transcript is a derived artifact, model choice locked to vendor, ~182x per-minute cost spread across providers.

drills.q: p50 response time is 420ms, yet CSAT dropped. Name the measurement mistake and two likely tail sources.
drills.a: Reporting the mean/median instead of p95/p99 â€” subjective experience anchors on worst turns; 400ms averages routinely hide 2.5s tails. Likely tail sources: endpointing policy on hesitant speakers, uncached prompts/cold starts, TTS vendor variance (tight-IQR vendors trade slower medians for fewer outliers), multi-vendor region hops.

drills.q: An enterprise support line wants a voice bot. Recommend an architecture and defend it against 'just use the realtime API.'
drills.a: Default cascaded: compliance needs per-stage transcripts (what was heard vs answered), domain fine-tuned models stay swappable, VPC residency possible, cost predictable ($0.0095-$0.17/min vs ~182x S2S spread).
