drills.a: Treat the adverse-action-reason-code requirement as a hard architectural constraint decided at model-selection time, not a bolt-on: use an interpretable-by-design model, or if a more complex model is justified by material accuracy gain, build and validate a stability-tested explanation pipeline BEFORE it generates real adverse decisions. Quantify the accuracy gain (reduced default losses) against the specific legal exposure (CFPB Circular 2026-03: complexity doesn't excuse compliance) -- invest in the explanation infrastructure up front rather than shipping first and fixing explainability later, since remediating live legally-deficient adverse-action notices (including liability for past decisions) is far more expensive.

drills.q: A quarter-end RWA figure doesn't reconcile against finance's general ledger, requiring manual adjustment entries. What's the likely root cause and fix?
drills.a: Likely cause: the risk-data-aggregation pipeline uses a different position snapshot time, netting logic, or currency-conversion path than the general ledger -- a classic BCBS 239 gap. Fix: establish a single golden-source data lineage feeding both finance and risk pipelines identically, with automated daily (not quarter-end-only) reconciliation controls.

drills.q: Design question: you're the Principal engineer for a regional bank that just crossed $100B in assets and picked up LCR/NSFR obligations for the first time. What's your first-quarter plan, and how do you handle a board deadline that arrives before the proper build is done?
drills.a: Start with data lineage and product-taxonomy mapping (classifying every deposit/loan/security into regulatory categories), not the ratio arithmetic -- that classification work is the real bottleneck. Build the mapping layer as versioned, testable, auditable code decoupled from the aggregation math. Stand up automated daily reconciliation against treasury/finance cash-flow systems immediately. If the board wants numbers in six weeks, deliver a clearly-labeled interim manual/semi-automated calculation with documented conservative assumptions and explicit gaps, continuing the proper automated build in parallel -- a precise-looking number on unreconciled data is worse than a clearly-caveated interim estimate.

drills.q: Design question: building a Monte Carlo pricer for a barrier option (knocks out if the underlying touches a level before expiry), what implementation risks go beyond standard vanilla Monte Carlo?
drills.a: Discrete-time simulation only checks the barrier at simulated steps, underestimating true knock-out probability for a continuously-monitored barrier (needs a Brownian-bridge correction or fine discretization with explicit convergence checks). Variance is much higher near the barrier (payoff highly sensitive to barrier touch), often needing importance sampling or a targeted control variate. Finite-difference Greeks near the barrier are numerically unstable due to payoff discontinuity and typically need a smoothed estimator.

drills.q: Design question: building a smart order router across 12 lit exchanges and 6 dark pools, what are the highest-priority modeling decisions in order, and how would you validate venue-toxicity scoring?
drills.a: Priority: (1) venue scoring via realized-vs-effective spread per venue to detect toxic/adverse-selection-heavy flow, (2) configurable risk-aversion (kappa) per order matching actual urgency, (3) real-time recalibration of impact/volatility parameters to avoid stale-calibration failure during regime shifts, (4) routing/tie-break mechanics last. Validate toxicity scores the same way as any predictive model: walk-forward, leakage-free backtesting -- track realized spread per venue out of sample and confirm 'less toxic' venues actually show smaller price-impact components after the fact, not just at the time scores were computed.

drills.q: What happened before SR 11-7, and what specific 2008-crisis failure directly motivated it?
drills.a: Before 2011, model risk was handled ad hoc within individual business lines with no unified firm-wide standard or mandated independent validation function. The 2008 crisis exposed this: deeply flawed mortgage-related valuation/rating models (MBS/CDO pricing and the ratings built on them) had no independent, empowered effective-challenge process forcing critical review before driving trillions of dollars of exposure. SR 11-7 (April 4, 2011) was the Fed/OCC's direct response.

drills.q: Design question: you're asked to build MRM-equivalent governance for a new agentic AI system that can autonomously initiate wire transfers, even though SR 26-2 formally excludes agentic AI from scope. What do you build, and how do you argue for the investment if leadership says it isn't legally required?
drills.a: Build proportional to actual business risk: inventory entry with exposure tracking (authority limit x transaction frequency), independent red-teaming for prompt-injection/unauthorized-action/guardrail-bypass, ongoing drift/anomaly monitoring, and a real effective-challenge mechanism with authority to pause the system. Argue on prudential/reputational-risk grounds independent of the regulatory carve-out -- reframe from 'compliance' to 'operational risk control for an autonomous system with financial authority,' the same segregation-of-duties and audit controls already required for a human employee with wire-transfer authority apply with equal force to a non-human agent with the same authority.

drills.q: Design question: building a fully systematic robo-advisor portfolio module across 15 asset classes with no explicit human return forecasts, would you use mean-variance optimization, risk parity, or a hybrid? What would change your answer if a tactical view was later added?
drills.a: Prefer risk parity (or minimum-variance with constraints) as the systematic default -- with no return forecasts, mean-variance would either fabricate noisy historical-mean estimates (walking into the estimation-error-maximization problem) or degenerate into risk parity anyway. If a tactical view is later added (e.g. 'emerging markets will outperform'), Black-Litterman is the right upgrade: it layers the specific view onto a market-equilibrium-implied prior with explicit confidence weighting, avoiding both ignoring the view (risk parity can't use it) and naive mean-variance's instability from overweighting an unshrunk view.

drills.q: A market-risk model passes backtesting cleanly for three years, then loses 8x its stated 99% VaR in a single crisis day. Was the model wrong?
drills.a: Not necessarily in a calibration sense -- a correctly calibrated 99% VaR model is expected to be exceeded ~1% of the time, and a large breach during a genuine unprecedented regime shift is consistent with correct calibration for the 'normal' regime it was built on while being structurally blind to a regime it never sampled. This is exactly why stress testing and reverse stress testing must be run as mandatory complements to VaR/ES, not replacements.

drills.q: Design question: building the nightly automated backtesting pipeline for nine trading desks, what would you compute and alert on beyond a single per-desk Kupiec pass/fail?
drills.a: Track both hypothetical (clean) and actual (dirty) P&L against prior VaR (FRTB requires both, and divergence between them is itself diagnostic of intraday risk-taking). Run Christoffersen's independence test and the combined conditional-coverage statistic alongside Kupiec to catch clustering. Alert proactively at 3 exceptions rather than waiting for the yellow-zone threshold at 5. Cross-check parametric/historical/Monte Carlo VaR against each other daily, alerting on divergence relative to each book's own trailing baseline spread (not a fixed threshold, since normal disagreement varies by asset class). Reconcile front-office vs independent risk VaR numbers daily as a standing control.

drills.q: When would you deliberately choose BIC over AIC for ARIMA order selection, and what's the tradeoff?
drills.a: When the goal is a parsimonious, interpretable model of the underlying process (e.g., explaining structure to a risk committee) rather than pure forecast accuracy -- BIC's k*ln(n) penalty is heavier at large n and more likely to recover the true sparse model. Tradeoff: AIC is asymptotically better for one-step-ahead prediction accuracy, so a BIC-selected model can underfit slightly relative to what minimizes forecast error.

drills.q: Why do you need to check whether a seasonal series' seasonal pattern is itself drifting before choosing classical decomposition vs STL?
drills.a: Classical decomposition estimates one fixed seasonal profile applied identically to every cycle across the whole series; if the seasonal shape genuinely evolves (e.g., a holiday peak shifting a week earlier over several years), classical decomposition blurs that real evolving structure into the noise/remainder term. STL's Loess-based approach lets the seasonal component adapt over time and captures it correctly.

drills.q: What's the practical risk of using a foundation model like TimesFM zero-shot on a financial return series, and how would you test it before trusting it?
drills.a: Foundation models are pretrained mostly on series with visible trend/seasonality (retail, web traffic); financial returns are closer to a low-signal, fat-tailed near-random-walk, so zero-shot uncertainty estimates may be miscalibrated. Test via walk-forward backtesting and check empirical coverage of quantile forecasts (does the 90% interval actually contain ~90% of realized values out of sample) before trusting it in production.

drills.q: Distinguish Prophet's changepoint trend from a Kalman local-level-plus-trend model -- aren't both just 'trend that can change'?
drills.a: Prophet's trend is piecewise linear with a small, regularized set of discrete changepoints -- a structural, sparse-jump story. A Kalman trend evolves continuously every period via process noise Q, a smooth random walk with no discrete changepoints. They can look similar smoothed but extrapolate differently: Prophet tends to extend the last growth rate more conservatively; a Kalman model with nontrivial Q keeps accumulating uncertainty every step into the future.

drills.q: Why does a good Deflated Sharpe Ratio not by itself mean a strategy is production-ready?
drills.a: DSR addresses statistical significance of the backtested Sharpe under multiple testing; it says nothing about transaction costs, market impact, capacity constraints, or regime shift after deployment -- those require separate diagnostics (market microstructure, risk metrics) even after a strategy clears the leakage and multiple-testing bars.

drills.q: In the Gemini 3.1 Pro '13 of 16 wins' launch (Feb 2026), what was omitted from the headline comparison table despite being in the underlying model card data?
drills.a: GDPval-AA enterprise-task Elo, where Claude models led by roughly 300 points -- present in the underlying data but absent from the headline comparison.

drills.q: Why can a benchmark ranking flip entirely between 'with tools' and 'without tools' conditions on the same benchmark (e.g. Humanity's Last Exam)?
drills.a: Tool access changes what the model can do to verify or compute an answer rather than reason it purely internally, so relative strengths (e.g. raw reasoning vs. tool-orchestration skill) can favor different models under each condition -- meaning a single headline number without the condition stated is incomplete.

drills.q: Design the four-stage process for choosing which frontier model powers a new agentic product.
drills.a: 1) Fast triage (hours): blank-cell/harness/tool-condition check, wait for one independent number. 2) Shortlist eval (days): held-out set from real production tasks, rubric tied to real outcomes, repeated runs. 3) Cost/license/ops gate: pricing at real volume, full license text, latency, availability track record. 4) Staged rollout: pinned version, small traffic percentage, continuous regression suite, widen only after real-traffic metrics confirm the offline signal.

drills.q: Explain the architectural bet Cartesia made with Sonic's state-space-model TTS versus a transformer-based competitor, and why it matters for p99.
drills.a: SSMs process sequences more efficiently than transformer attention, giving Sonic consistently low latency including at the tail (p99), not just a good median -- Sonic 3.5 reports 75-90ms time-to-first-audio, which matters because p99 determines the worst-case caller experience, not the average one.

drills.q: A passage copies the user's question verbatim and asserts a false answer. Why might dense retrieval and a cross-encoder both promote it?
drills.a: It is engineered for relevance: the query text maximizes embedding similarity, and the cross-encoder sees a passage that appears to answer the question. Neither mechanism independently checks truth or source authority.

drills.q: Name the fields you would require before allowing a document into a security-sensitive RAG corpus.
drills.a: Source identity, owner, ingestion time, version, content hash, extraction method/confidence, trust tier, ACL scope, and a review or quarantine state. The exact schema can vary, but provenance and authorization cannot be optional.

drills.q: Why is 'we use a prompt telling the model to ignore instructions in documents' not a complete answer?
drills.a: The document and instruction still share a token stream, so the model can be fooled by instruction-shaped or indirect content. It is a useful reduction, not a deterministic boundary; isolate content and enforce trust outside the model.

drills.q: Design the minimum experiment that can claim a defense reduced poisoning risk.
drills.a: Freeze a corpus and question set, create clean and attack conditions, verify the attack lands at the intended dose, run one defense change per arm, use deterministic scoring, and report correct/attacked/abstained/failed plus clean false positives and latency.

drills.q: Three low-authority copies claim X and one current policy says Y. Why is majority voting the wrong resolver?
drills.a: Copies are not independent authority. An attacker can cheaply multiply them, so vote count becomes an attacker-controlled variable. Resolve by source tier and freshness, or abstain when trusted sources conflict.

drills.q: What failure does isolated passage reading solve, and what failure does it not solve?
drills.a: It prevents candidate passages from instructing or arguing with one another inside a shared prompt. It does not prove a passage is truthful; a poison can still produce a verified false claim, so provenance-based resolution is required afterward.

drills.q: A guard threshold of 0.9 misses a reordered poison scoring 0.5 but catches legitimate FAQ text scoring 1.0. What should you do?
drills.a: Do not simply lower the threshold. The distributions overlap, so threshold tuning cannot separate them. Keep the measured limitation, add structural/provenance defenses, and retain the FAQ as a false-positive control.

drills.q: How do you prevent an eval from rewarding a system that abstains on every poisoned question?
drills.a: Score utility and safety separately. Abstention can be correct on an attack, but it must not receive the same credit as recovering the correct answer; report clean answer rate, poisoned-case abstention, attacked rate, and failures.

drills.q: A poisoned document was indexed for six hours. Walk through incident response.
drills.a: Quarantine the exact version and preserve its hash and provenance; block retrieval; identify affected queries, answers, users, and downstream actions; invalidate caches; restore from a trusted snapshot or reindex; notify owners if exposure occurred; add the attack to the permanent regression suite.

drills.q: How would you distinguish a retrieval-poisoning regression from a generation hallucination?
drills.a: Log candidate IDs, ranks, trust metadata, isolated claims, resolver decisions, and final citations. If the poison reached the reader and the resolver selected it, the fault is retrieval integrity/resolution. If trusted evidence was present but the model invented a claim, it is generation faithfulness.

drills.q: What should the system do when a high-authority current policy and a lower-authority newer ticket disagree?
drills.a: Use an explicit policy: authority tier first only if the policy says it outranks freshness; otherwise mark the conflict and abstain or route to a human. Never let an opaque LLM decide from prose without recording the evidence and rule applied.

drills.q: Why is a poisoned-RAG benchmark invalid if the attack never enters top-k?
drills.a: Because the defense was never tested. A zero attack-success rate could mean the defense worked, or merely that the attack construction was too weak. An attack-landing gate must be a prerequisite to scoring the defensive arm.

drills.q: Explain an RLM in one sentence to an interviewer.
drills.a: It keeps a long prompt outside the model as a programmable data environment and lets the model inspect, decompose, and recursively solve selected slices instead of processing the entire prompt in one context.

drills.q: Why does a 1M-token context window not eliminate context engineering?
drills.a: Nominal capacity is not uniform reasoning quality. Attention dilution and context rot can reduce recall or synthesis quality while the input still fits, and cost/latency remain material.

drills.q: Contrast RLM with a vector database retriever.
drills.a: A vector retriever selects chunks using an index and similarity metric. An RLM exposes the prompt as data that the model can search, slice, inspect, and recursively process, which can support exact filters and task-specific exploration without pre-indexing.

drills.q: Design the environment API for an RLM processing 5,000 support tickets.
drills.a: Expose bounded peek, regex/keyword search, partition by ticket, typed child calls, aggregation, and provenance. Deny arbitrary filesystem/network access; cap depth, fan-out, tokens, wall time, and output size.

drills.q: Why is just recursively calling the model on every chunk a bad design?
drills.a: It creates a fan-out cost explosion and may duplicate work. First filter or partition programmatically, then call only on relevant slices, use structured outputs, parallelize safely, and enforce cumulative budgets.

drills.q: What observability proves an RLM is bounded?
drills.a: Trace parent-child call relationships and record recursion depth, fan-out, selected byte/token ranges, child prompt/completion tokens, cumulative cost, wall time, cancellations, retries, and final aggregation status.

drills.q: A child call times out after its siblings completed. What should the parent do?
drills.a: Represent the timeout as a typed partial failure, preserve which slice was missing, apply a policy such as retry once or return a bounded incomplete result, and never silently treat missing evidence as negative evidence.

drills.q: When would RLM be worse than RAG?
drills.a: For a stable corpus with high reuse, a well-tuned retriever and cache may be cheaper and faster. RLM adds model-call orchestration and can repeatedly scan data; use it when programmatic exploration or long-context degradation is the actual bottleneck.

drills.q: How do you prevent a malicious document from turning an RLM into an agent?
drills.a: Keep the environment capabilities narrow and deterministic, mark document text as untrusted data, validate all tool and child-call arguments outside the model, sandbox code, deny arbitrary egress, and apply hard budgets and audit logging.

drills.q: How would you evaluate RLM against compaction fairly?
drills.a: Use identical task inputs, model/provider, output contract, and quality rubric. Compare answer correctness and evidence coverage while separately reporting model calls, input/output tokens, wall time, cache effects, failure rate, and human review cost.

drills.q: Why can RLM improve a shorter prompt too, not just an oversized one?
drills.a: It can enforce deliberate programmatic search and decomposition instead of asking attention to scan everything. The benefit is selective computation and structure, not merely fitting beyond a context limit.

drills.q: What is the principal-level migration path from a vanilla long-context system to RLM?
drills.a: Instrument context-length versus quality first, identify tasks with context rot, add a read-only external environment and deterministic slice tools, introduce typed child calls behind a feature flag, compare against the old path on a fixed eval set, then expand only if quality/cost/latency justify the operational complexity.
